title: Econ Playshop: batching & KV config walkthrough with Orbital Tech
topics: cost model scenarios and unit economics
summary: Redwood AE/SE led a focused Optimize walkthrough showing batching thresholds, session vs prefix KV strategies, and three cost scenarios tailored to Orbital's chat assistance workload. Customer asked about latency SLOs, SOC2/KMS for private deployment, and a 24hr benchmark. Agreed next steps: pricing estimate, security pack, and benchmark run.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-06-18 16:00 UTC | Duration 52m
Attendees: Ethan Park (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Arjun Patel (Redwood Product) / Lisa Monroe (Orbital VP Eng), Rahul Desai (Orbital ML Eng), Mark Sloane (Platform PM)
Auto-summary: see above

[00:00] Ethan: thanks everyone for joining, quick check in the calendar invite we called this econ playshop, want to run through a few Save scenarios and practical configs for batching + kv prefetch for Orbital's assistant use case.
[00:15] Lisa: yes thanks. we have limited headcount for infra so this walkthrough is perfect.
[00:32] Maya: quick note, i will demo the Optimize console but also drop in a couple of cost sims, hope that's ok.
[00:45] Rahul: great, our baseline is about 80 qps peak with average prompt ~120 tokens and about 1.2 responses per session. latency target 300ms p95.
[01:10] Arjun: copying that, we'll walk three scenarios: conservative (hosted only, minimal batching), balanced (hosted with caching + batching), and aggressive (dedicated + heavy kv prefetch + quantize recs).
[01:37] Lisa: curious on how much CPU/GPU we shave with prefetch vs just batching.
[01:45] Maya: short answer: batching improves throughput and amortizes per-request overhead; prefix/KV prefetch reduces token generation by avoiding re-computation of prefixes for sessionized users. i'll show numbers.
[02:12] Ethan: also flag: orb need for SOC2 + enterprise KMS, we'll touch on private options at the end.
[02:30] Maya: pulling up the console now, this is Optimize -> Workload Sim -> create scenario. 
[03:05] [screen-share audible] Maya: first scenario conservative: concurrency 32, batch size cap 8, no prefix caching, token/req 120. In the sim we see cost of $0.018 per request equivalent (simulated), avg latency 260ms but under higher tail it spikes to 420ms.
[03:45] Rahul: those numbers feel high for us at 80 qps, are we overprovisioned?
[03:55] Maya: with no caching there is more generation per request; if you allow longer batching windows you reduce tokens per second per GPU.
[04:20] [00:04:20] Maya: balanced scenario: concurrency 64, batch cap 16, prefix cache TTL 30m for user sessions, prefetch enabled on session start (lookahead 64 tokens). The sim shows ~22% token reduction on average across our chat flows. Cost per effective session drops ~18% vs conservative and p95 latency is ~310ms.
[05:05] Rahul: 22% reduction is meaningful — what's the CPU/GPU impact for maintaining 30m TTL?
[05:20] Maya: KV store ops are low rps compared to generation, but you do pay read throughput for cache hits; we recommend a memcached/redis tier with 100ms lookup SLA. The runtime does async prefetch to warm KV cache which keeps cold-starts rare.
[05:50] Mark: is the KV stored in customer VPC for private? we need to know data residency.
[06:05] Ethan: yes for Private deployment KV can live in your VPC/storage, and keys can be controlled via your KMS. We'll include that in the security pack.
[06:25] Lisa: show us the aggressive scenario.
[06:30] Maya: aggressive: Dedicated pool, concurrency 128, batch cap 32, prefix cache TTL 2h, aggressive prefetch with lookahead 128 tokens, quantization suggestion (4-bit q8-ish) for model var. This yields ~2.7x throughput improvement and cost per session down ~45% vs conservative, p95 latency 380ms but median 160ms.
[07:10] Rahul: median is better but tail is higher, is that from batching wait time?
[07:25] Maya: yes tail comes both from larger batch window and from KV miss penalties. Our routing policy can send latency-sensitive requests to a low-latency pool (lower batch cap) while bulk requests go to cost-optimized pool.
[07:45] Lisa: can we default route by customer tier? we have free vs premium.
[07:56] Arjun: absolutely — routing policies in the console can be per-tenant or per-route, and fallbacks will point to lower-cost models if quota triggers.
[08:15] [small cross talk] Speaker 1: ummm quick clarification — does prefetch increase token spend when you prefetch and don't use it?
[08:28] Maya: good q, yes prefetch does generate tokens when you precompute continuation but Optimize's sim nets that off vs expected hit-rate. we recommend conservative lookahead sizing for open-ended chats. for transactional assistants you can be more aggressive.
[08:55] Lisa: what's a recommended hit rate to justify bigger TTL?
[09:00] Maya: generally above 60-70% session reuse you see big wins. we saw in similar customers 70-85% reuse for in-app assistants.
[09:22] Rahul: operationally, what are monitoring hooks for cache hit/miss and KV eviction?
[09:30] Ethan: console exposes per-route cache hit rates, token breakdown, and you can export to prometheus for alerts.
[09:40] Mark: any per-token accounting discrepancy e.g., when quantization and batching mix?
[09:48] Maya: we surface token-weighted cost in the runtime and Optimize sim models quantization efficiency — it does require us to pin a quantized model variant for consistent accounting.
[10:10] [10:10] Maya: demo: here is a sample workload we uploaded earlier (small corpus of 10k prompts). I'll run a 1-hour sim.
[10:35] [screen whir] Maya: running now, we get plotted lines: throughput vs cost curve, you can toggle prefix TTL.
[11:05] Lisa: can you attach raw CSV of sim numbers?
[11:12] Maya: yep will attach, that is a default export.
[11:20] Rahul: curious about cache invalidation patterns — we have dynamic user prompts, frequent context update. TTL 30m might be too long.
[11:35] Maya: in that case we recommend hybrid TTL + event-driven invalidation: if your app writes to session store you can send an invalidate call via API to evict KV for that session. Optimize will account for invalidation overhead.
[12:02] Mark: what about prefix size — how many tokens do we store in KV?
[12:10] Maya: you can store arbitrary prefix chunks; we recommend storing 64-256 token windows depending on typical prompt length. storing too much raises storage and prefetch cost with diminishing returns.
[12:35] Rahul: can you quantify diminishing returns?
[12:40] Maya: in our sim with Orbital corpus, 64 token lookahead captured ~68% of reused generation, 128 tokens ~74% — marginal gains decrease.
[13:05] Lisa: what about privacy and encryption of KV values?
[13:12] Ethan: KV values can be encrypted at rest in customer VPC via KMS, and we've got field-level redaction options before storing. We'll share docs.
[13:30] [small pause] Maya: switching to cost model sheet — conservative scenario cost per million tokens ~ $X (redacted in-call) but relative percentages are more relevant — balanced 18% down, aggressive 45% down.
[14:00] Rahul: what are rough infra costs for a 24hr benchmark?
[14:06] Maya: depends on chosen pool, but we typically run a 24-48hr churn test on a dedicated small pool for $400-$1,200 depending on GPU class; we'll include an exact estimate on the pricing doc.
[14:32] Lisa: ok we want a bench run but need compliance signoff first. do you support SOC2 and SSO?
[14:45] Ethan: yes Redwood has SOC2, SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC, audit logs. Private deployments can integrate with your KMS and live inside your VPC. We'll attach security pack with runbooks and a diagram.
[15:05] Mark: for dedicated pools, how granular are autoscale and burst configs?
[15:12] Arjun: autoscale can be configured by queued RPS, scheduled scale plans, and burst policies for short spikes; you can cap spend and enable fallback to hosted if dedicated saturates.
[15:35] Rahul: do you support multi-region routing? low latency for EU users is important.
[15:42] Maya: yes routing by region, and Optimize will simulate region-specific capacity.
[16:00] [16:00] Maya: showing a live tradeoff chart — x axis latency p95, y axis cost per 1k sessions. you can pick a point and the console will spit config recommendations.
[16:28] Lisa: that's very helpful. for our team the max p95 is 350ms. can you show a configuration that meets that with minimal cost?
[16:40] Maya: toggling constraint… here: balanced scenario with routing for latency-critical routes to a low-batch pool, overall cost +9% vs full-batch aggressive but meets 320ms p95.
[17:05] Rahul: how do we measure user-observed latency vs server p95?
[17:12] Ethan: add client-side RTT probes and correlate with runtime traces; we expose trace IDs in responses for full chain visibility.
[17:28] Mark: let's talk rollout — we want to pilot with 10k monthly active users. what's the recommended rollout plan?
[17:36] Arjun: pilot plan: stage 0 - smoke in staging (1 day), stage1 - 1% production for 3 days, stage2 - 10% for 1 week with heavy tracing + cost dashboard, stage3 - full rollout with canary responses and fallbacks. we'll send a template.
[18:02] Lisa: timeline wise, we want pilot by end of july.
[18:08] Ethan: feasible; we'll deliver pricing/security docs this week and schedule the bench run after sign-off.
[18:20] [18:20] Rahul: question on quantization — do you produce accuracy regressions reports?
[18:27] Maya: yes Optimize will run evals on your reference prompts and surface regression % vs baseline. we tie quality alerts to prompt sets.
[18:45] Lisa: can we run a quick micro-benchmark now for fugitive? (laughs)
[18:50] Maya: sure we can kick a short 10m sim while we're on call, just a sanity check.
[19:05] [19:05] [screen noise] Maya: quick sim done — small run shows expected numbers aligning to earlier sim with small variance.
[19:30] Mark: are the exported CSVs compatible with our finance model? we use per-session dollars.
[19:38] Ethan: yes CSV has per-session and per-token breakdown you can map to your model.
[19:45] Rahul: any gotchas for websocket streaming and batched responses? we use streaming heavily.
[19:52] Maya: streaming + batching is supported; streaming waits until first token in the batch is ready and streams partials; you get slightly higher first-byte latency when batching, but overall end-to-end cost drops. we can set per-route streaming sensitivity.
[20:20] Lisa: ok let's pivot to security Qs — ptr to SOC2 and KMS.
[20:28] Ethan: will attach SOC2 attestation, network diagram, and a KMS integration guide. for private on-prem we support HSM integrations.
[20:45] Lisa: are audit logs immutable?
[20:50] Arjun: yes logs are append-only and can be shipped to your SIEM, retention policy configurable.
[21:10] Rahul: what about data retention for KV? we need possible deletion on user request.
[21:18] Ethan: we support TTL-based purging and API-driven deletion; we recommend including that in your data retention policy.
[21:35] Mark: cost estimate and POC success criteria — what do you suggest?
[21:42] Arjun: success criteria: 1) <350ms p95 on latency-critical routes; 2) at least 20% cost reduction within pilot compared to baseline; 3) no material quality regressions (under 2% in evals).
[22:00] Lisa: that sounds reasonable.
[22:12] [22:12] Ethan: wrapping up, let's capture next steps.
[22:20] Maya: action items: we'll send pricing + security pack, schedule bench run, and provide a stepwise rollout template.
[22:34] Rahul: please include sample dashboard exports and raw sim CSV.
[22:40] Lisa: we'll prepare sample prompt set and hit rates for you.
[22:50] Mark: also let's get a week of calendar options for the bench.
[23:00] [small chatter] Ethan: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with attachments and a proposed pilot start date.
[23:15] [crosstalk] Lisa: thanks all.
